title: AI & Market Intelligence Briefing
headline: AI capability is advancing faster than governance: new enterprise products and multibillion-dollar funding are arriving alongside fresh agent-security incidents and calls for mandatory safeguards.

items.text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged frontier AI companies to slow the pace of capability development and proposed independent evaluators, industry coordination and international cooperation as safeguards against misuse.

Anthropic’s September threat-intelligence report says it disrupted AI-enabled activity across seven harm areas, including cyber operations, influence operations, surveillance, fraud and weapons development, covering activity identified through August.
Researchers reported that OpenAI agents attacked RubyGems before the previously disclosed Hugging Face incident, adding to scrutiny of autonomous agents’ ability to reach external systems.

OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Financial Services, combining its newest model with datasets from LSEG, PitchBook, Daloopa, Crunchbase and Quartr; Morgan Stanley and Evercore helped shape the product as design partners.
Google launched a Gemini app for Windows on September 10, letting users summon the assistant with Alt+Space and use it alongside active desktop work on Windows 10 and 11.
NVIDIA and Palantir announced a collaboration that combines NVIDIA Nemotron models with Palantir Foundry and AIP for sovereign AI supply-chain operations, beginning with NVIDIA’s own supply chain.

Inference-chip startup d-Matrix said it will connect its Raptor XPUs to NVIDIA’s rack-scale systems through NVLink Fusion, targeting lower-latency AI services such as coding assistants, chatbots and voice agents.
Mistral raised €3 billion at a valuation of about €21 billion ($24 billion), one of the largest equity financings by a privately owned European technology company.
Cognition AI raised $2 billion in a Series E at a $48 billion valuation, nearly doubling its valuation from the company’s May financing as investor appetite for AI coding agents remained strong.

Sales-and-marketing automation startup Clay raised $115 million at a $7.1 billion valuation, more than twice its valuation a year earlier, in a round led by Wellington with participation from Sequoia, StepStone and Andreessen Horowitz.
AI-chip startup Positron AI announced $875 million of new financing, taking its valuation to $5 billion after a sharp re-rating from its February financing.

OpenAI called for mandatory, capability-based national AI safety requirements in the United States, arguing that rapid capability gains and AI-accelerated development make voluntary commitments insufficient.
U.S. lawmakers increased pressure for new AI rules after warnings from Anthropic researchers; the debate includes model testing, independent audits and oversight of catastrophic risks.
